UnitStatement: DEL-03-03 (DeliverableID) is the Harness API and SSE Compatibility Adapter, under PackageID PKG-03 Runtime Engine Contract and Turn Lifecycle.

ResponsibleParty for DEL-03-03 is TBD.
DEL-03-03's primary subject is a compatibility adapter for harness API routes and browser-facing SSE event names while runtime policy moves behind services.
The in-scope API surface is the harness routes /api/harness/session/create, /session/boot, /session/list, /session/[id], /turn, /interrupt, and /scaffold.
/api/harness/turn remains a transport adapter that validates request shape, obtains the session lock, forwards input to TurnEngine, writes SSE, and handles cleanup.
Browser SSE event names are session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit.
Browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents are separate contracts; UI events remain stable and compact (K-EVENT-1, FR-074).
SDK messages are not the browser contract or canonical persisted event contract; provider/SDK fields belong at adapter metadata boundaries.
Anticipated artifacts are route adapter tests, SSE compatibility fixtures, and UI event contract docs.
Compatibility condition: existing route shapes and SSE event names remain stable during SDK adoption and TurnEngine extraction.
Active-turn condition: only one active turn may run per session; concurrent turn attempts return TURN_IN_PROGRESS (FR-018).
Stream termination condition: the stream terminates with a process-level completion/error signal unless the client disconnects.
Disconnect condition: client disconnect cleanup records cancellation once the event log exists.
docs/PRD.md is locally accessible but recorded as HASH_MISMATCH (REF-006); PRD-derived details are source-state-warning context, not newly accepted immutable truth.
Route adapter layer: keep /api/harness/turn as the SSE transport adapter; runtime policy belongs behind TurnEngine and engine contract services (FR-071).
SSE encoder/fixture layer: preserve the named SSE events listed in SPEC/TYPES/PRD; additional tool progress events require UI compatibility handling.
UI/runtime mapper boundary: map SDK messages into browser UIEvents and richer persisted HarnessEvents without exposing SDK message names as public UI contract (FR-116).
Test artifacts: build route adapter tests, SSE compatibility fixtures, and UI event contract docs; exact fixture payloads are TBD pending current implementation capture.

This deliverable protects the browser-facing harness contract while internal runtime ownership changes, keeping /api/harness/* and named SSE events stable for the UI.
Runtime responsibilities are taken over behind the boundary by TurnEngine, AgentEnginePort, SDK message mapping, and persisted HarnessEvent records.
Preserve the browser contract: treat existing /api/harness/* route shapes and named SSE events as compatibility surfaces and do not rename stable SSE events during the runtime pivot.
Keep route and runtime ownership separate: /api/harness/turn should validate, lock, encode SSE, forward to TurnEngine, and handle cleanup, not own runtime policy (FR-071).
Keep SDK details behind adapters: SDK message names, session IDs, transcript paths, permission modes, and tool names are adapter metadata, not public Chirality UI contracts.
Treat UI and audit records differently: browser UIEvents stay compact and compatible while persisted HarnessEvents can be richer, versioned, and audit-oriented (K-EVENT-1).
Verify compatibility with fixtures: prefer captured route/SSE fixtures and replay tests over prose-only review; exact existing payload fixtures are TBD.
docs/PRD.md is a useful local source for the runtime pivot but is recorded as HASH_MISMATCH; keep PRD-derived details traceable and avoid treating unsupported details as immutable truth.
The stable event-name list is source-backed across SPEC, TYPES, and PRD: session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, process:exit.
Compatibility should be tested from the browser-facing side: route shapes, status codes, SSE names, payload fields, and terminal/error behavior observable by existing UI consumers.
New internal HarnessEvent categories or SDK metadata should not force UI payload churn unless an explicit compatibility layer is documented and tested.
Sibling deliverable ownership: active-turn locking and TurnEngine internals belong to DEL-03-02; interrupt/cancel cleanup and terminal outcome persistence belong to DEL-03-04 and PKG-05.
Preserving route/SSE compatibility while refactoring internals reduces UI breakage during SDK adoption but may constrain ideal internal API shape; mitigate by keeping adapters thin and source-backed.
Keeping UIEvent compact and separate from HarnessEvent lets runtime audit expand without browser churn but requires mapper discipline enforced by tests rejecting SDK-shaped public leakage.

Capturing exact current route fixtures before implementation changes makes compatibility measurable but can ossify accidental behavior; mitigate by documenting which fields are contractual versus compatibility-only TBD.
Allowing additional tool progress events only with compatibility handling enables richer future UI feedback but could surprise older clients; mitigate via opt-in or backward-compatible consumption.

Compatibility handling for additional tool progress events must name one accepted mode per event: ignored safely by existing clients, consumed only by opt-in UI behavior, or carried through a documented backward-compatible path.

Fixture field class Contractual: named by SPEC, TYPES, CONTRACT, or PRD as part of the public route, SSE, UIEvent, or product-owned HarnessEvent contract, evidenced by source section plus fixture assertion.

Fixture field class Compatibility-only: present in captured current behavior but not source-backed as a required public contract, evidenced by fixture path, implementation baseline SHA, and retention rationale.

Fixture field class Adapter metadata: provider/SDK identifiers, message names, transcript paths, session IDs, permission modes, or tool names appearing only behind adapter boundaries (DIRECTIVE 2.10, K-ENGINE-4).
Fixture field class TBD: a field that cannot yet be classified because current implementation capture or source location is unavailable, recorded with the required source or capture action.

The DEL-03-03 specification covers the compatibility adapter contract for harness API routes and browser-facing SSE events during the runtime-engine pivot.
Spec scope: preserving /api/harness/* route shapes during SDK adoption and TurnEngine extraction.
Spec scope: keeping /api/harness/turn as the SSE transport adapter rather than the owner of runtime policy.
Spec scope: preserving browser SSE event names and compact UIEvent semantics.
Spec scope: separating browser UIEvents from persisted HarnessEvents.
Spec scope: defining route adapter tests, SSE compatibility fixtures, and UI event contract documentation.
Out of scope: SDK-specific message translation internals except where they must not leak into the browser contract.
Out of scope: TurnEngine lifecycle ownership and session locking internals, owned primarily by DEL-03-02.
Out of scope: interrupt/cancel terminal outcome handling, owned primarily by DEL-03-04.
Out of scope: persisted event schema implementation, owned primarily by PKG-05, except compatibility assertions that UI and runtime event contracts remain separate.

REQ-001: the adapter shall preserve the existing /api/harness/* route shapes during SDK adoption and TurnEngine extraction; exact existing request/response schemas are TBD pending implementation fixture capture.

REQ-002: /api/harness/turn shall remain a transport adapter responsible for request validation, session locking, attachment option forwarding where applicable, SSE encoding, cancellation cleanup, and error response handling.

REQ-003: browser-facing turn streams shall emit compatible named SSE events session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit; event ordering is unconstrained except where source/fixtures establish an order.
REQ-004: the SSE stream shall terminate with a process-level completion/error signal unless the client disconnects and cancel cleanup runs.
REQ-005: browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents shall remain separate contracts; persisted events may be richer and versioned, but UI events remain compact and compatible.

REQ-006: SDK messages shall not be treated as the browser or canonical persisted event contract; the mapper boundary is expected to be frontend/src/lib/harness/sdk-message-mapper.ts during R1, or a documented equivalent.

REQ-007: additional tool progress events may be introduced only with UI compatibility handling so older clients ignore them safely, handle them via opt-in UI behavior, or receive them through a documented backward-compatible path.
REQ-008: the compatibility kit shall include route adapter tests, SSE compatibility fixtures, and UI event contract docs.
REQ-009: PRD-derived requirements shall carry a source-state warning until the REF-006 hash mismatch is resolved.
REQ-010: the route adapter test index shall map each in-scope /api/harness/* route to a fixture path or TBD capture status before exact compatibility assertions are closed.
Standard: product-owned runtime contract requires adapter behavior to serve Chirality-owned AgentEnginePort/RuntimeEngineContract, not SDK public semantics (DIRECTIVE 2.8/2.10, SPEC 10).
Standard: browser SSE event contract defines the required event names and stream termination behavior (SPEC 11, TYPES 7.4, PRD 9.3).
Standard: harness API route contract defines the /api/harness/* route catalog and stability expectation (SPEC 17.1, PRD 9.1).
Standard: runtime/audit event separation keeps browser UIEvent and persisted HarnessEvent as distinct contracts (CONTRACT 1.5, PRD 8.12).
Standard: test/validation expectations require the route stream to be unchanged after SDK-backed TurnEngine extraction, with SDK message mapper coverage (PRD 12.5/12.6).
